title: The Political Economy of Energy Transitions in the Global South: Domestic Coalitions, State Capacity, and the Structural Constraints of Climate Finance 2. Authors
summary: Why do energy transitions in the Global South advance unevenly when renewable technologies are cost-competitive and international climate finance is on offer? I argue that outcomes depend on the interaction of two variables: the political settlement that determines whether incumbent fossil fuel interests are compensated, bypassed or displaced, and the position of the state within a hierarchical international financial system, which conditions whether external finance widens or narrows fiscal space. Using a structured, focused comparison of South Africa, India and the lithium-producing states of Chile, Argentina and Bolivia, based on official programme, audit, statistical and regulatory records, I identify three mechanisms. In South Africa, 42 per cent of USD 13.92 billion in Just Energy Transition Partnership pledges had been allocated by December 2025; sovereign policy loans were the only instrument allocated in full, while concessional loans intended for the state utility were held back by its borrowing restrictions. In India, nine state-owned energy firms invested INR 2.33 trillion in fossil fuels and INR 0.30 trillion in clean energy in fiscal year 2025, and state distribution companies returned to long-term coal contracts while about 42 GW of tendered renewable capacity lacked buyers. In the lithium triangle, the state's share of rents follows state capacity and business power, and remains exposed to a fall in the average price of battery-grade lithium carbonate from USD 63,700 per tonne in 2022 to USD 9,000 in 2025. The article shows how the composition and channel of climate finance, rather than its headline volume, shape domestic transition politics.

title: INNOVATIVE SUPPLY CHAIN MODELS FOR ENHANCING FOOD SECURITY AND ECONOMIC GROWTH IN NIGERIA
summary: Food security remains a critical challenge in Nigeria, exacerbated by population growth, infrastructural deficits, and climate variability. Inefficient supply chains severely hinder agricultural productivity and market access for farmers. This paper explores innovative supply chain models to address these issues and spur economic growth. It emphasizes collaborative networks, digital platforms, and public-private partnerships to strengthen agricultural value chains. Integrating cold storage, decentralized warehousing, and data-driven insights can reduce post-harvest losses, stabilize food availability, and regulate prices. Technologies like blockchain and IoT enhance traceability, build consumer trust, and attract agribusiness investments. Drawing on case studies from Sub-Saharan Africa, the study shows how modernized supply chains boost food security, generate employment, and contribute to GDP. Policy recommendations are provided to scale sustainable, technology-driven solutions across Nigeria’s agricultural sector. title: The emerging role of smart supply chain as a stabilizer: evidence from the emotion management
summary: Purpose This study explores how smart supply chains mitigate managers' excessive positive and negative emotions, focusing on the mediating role of social attention and moderating role of collaborative culture, aiming to reveal how enterprises can improve decision-making and support sustainable operations via supply chain management. Design/methodology/approach Based on Affective Events Theory and Socio-Technical Theory, we employ regression analysis and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis to examine the relationship and underlying mechanisms between smart supply chains and managers' emotions. Findings The smart supply chain curbs both managers' excessive positive and negative emotions. Corporate social attention strongly mediates and cooperative culture notably moderates its relation with managers' emotions. Additionally, SSC-driven, SSC-led, and SA-driven types are effective emotion-suppressing configurations. Originality/value This study pioneers in viewing smart supply chains as emotional stabilizers, merging emotion regulation theory with supply chain intelligence. It offers practical insights for reducing negative emotions, improving decisions, and supporting sustainability, deepening knowledge of intelligent supply chains' impact on managerial emotions.

title: How Chinese Import Competition Affected American Workers, Communities, and Supply Chains
summary: This paper examines how the rise in Chinese imports affected the U.S. in several ways. On one hand, Americans got lower prices, and companies had to find ways to compete and become more efficient. But at the same time, many manufacturing workers and communities were hit hard by increased import competition. Applying economic theory, China shock research, and case studies like the furniture industry in High Point, North Carolina, this paper examines how these benefits and costs were distributed across consumers, workers, and communities. It also considers how the decline of domestic manufacturing contributed to greater dependence on Chinese supply chains, thus creating new economic risks. The paper argues that trade was not the only issue. The larger problem was that the U.S. was not prepared to help the workers and communities that were most affected. Therefore, it ultimately considers to what extent a country can benefit from trade while also addressing the costs experienced by those who lose the most from it.

title: Patient Data Management In A Commercial Clinic: Audit, Segmentation, And Data Strategy
summary: This article examines data management methods in a commercial medical organization. Based on an audit of the information infrastructure of a multidisciplinary clinic, the study describes procedures for patient data profiling and deduplication, develops a KPI system using the Balanced Scorecard methodology, constructs an RFM segmentation model to identify patients at high risk of churn, and proposes a phased data strategy for transitioning toward data-driven management. The paper also provides a systematic review of Data Governance frameworks and digital transformation practices in healthcare, contextualizing the clinic-level findings within broader trends in health data management.

title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF A TRADING ENTERPRISE: THE ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN BUSINESS PROCESS REENGINEERING
summary: The digital transformation of contemporary retail enterprises is one of the defining factors of their competitiveness and adaptation to a changing market environment. The rapid development of artificial intelligence methods has opened new opportunities for a fundamental rethinking of retail business processes – from inventory management and demand forecasting to personalised customer service and dynamic pricing. The article systematises the theoretical foundations and analyses the practical experience of applying artificial intelligence methods for the reengineering of retail business processes. The essence of digital transformation is defined as a systemic phenomenon that involves simultaneous changes in operating models, the technological platform, and organisational culture, rather than the isolated implementation of individual digital tools. Based on the analysis of digital maturity levels, a differentiated approach to the integration of artificial intelligence is substantiated, depending on the enterprise’s readiness and available data infrastructure. The role of business process reengineering is revealed as a methodological mechanism of digital transformation that prevents the automation of inefficient processes. Artificial intelligence methods are grouped according to their applicability to typical retail business processes. International and domestic experience of artificial intelligence implementation in retail chains is analysed. Key prerequisites for the successful integration of artificial intelligence solutions are formulated, and a conceptual four-layer integration model is proposed, encompassing the data, analytical, decision-making, and managerial levels. The practical value of the work lies in the possibility of applying the developed tools by managers of retail enterprises for self-diagnostics and the justification of managerial decisions.

title: Governance, CSR, and Leverage on Financial Distress in Indonesian Consumer Cyclicals
summary: Fluctuations in macroeconomic conditions and consumer purchasing capacity render firms in the consumer cyclical sector particularly susceptible to financial distress. Although the sector's index posted an upward trajectory throughout the observation window, such aggregate expansion offers no assurance that individual issuers maintain sound financial footing. Drawing on 116 firm-year observations from 29 consumer cyclical firms listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange across 2022-2025, this inquiry appraises how institutional ownership, independent commissioners, audit committee independence, corporate social responsibility (CSR) disclosure, and leverage relate to financial distress, operationalized through the Altman Z-Score, wherein elevated values signify a more robust financial standing and diminished vulnerability to failure. Sample selection followed a purposive sampling scheme, with panel-data regression estimated under a random-effects specification. Findings reveal that institutional ownership, independent commissioners, audit committee independence, and CSR disclosure bear no discernible statistical linkage to the Z-Score, whereas leverage registers a pronounced inverse relationship, implying that intensified debt reliance coincides with a depressed Z-Score and heightened distress exposure. Jointly, the five predictors exert a collectively significant influence on Z-Score variation, underscoring the ambiguous role of governance and CSR mechanisms while positioning leverage as the most consequential determinant of financial vulnerability among the firms examined

title: ECONOMIC CYBER-ESPIONAGE IN THE CONTEXT OF GLOBAL DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AND THE WAR IN UKRAINE: RISKS TO ECONOMIC SECURITY, CYBER THREATS AND REGULATORY CHALLENGES
summary: This article examines economic cyber-espionage as a systemic threat to economic security, considering it in the context of global digital transformation and the growing reliance of modern economies on information technology. It explores how cyber-espionage has evolved from an intelligence-related activity to become an instrument of economic competition, technological rivalry and geopolitical influence. Particular attention is paid to the mechanisms involved in obtaining confidential commercial information, intellectual property, technological developments and strategic economic data by exploiting vulnerabilities in digital infrastructures. The research identifies the key features of economic cyber-espionage, such as its transnational nature, the anonymity of the perpetrators, the long-term persistence of cyber operations and the involvement of state-sponsored advanced persistent threat (APT) groups. The article analyses the economic consequences of cyber-espionage, including losses associated with intellectual property theft, disruption to innovation processes, reduced competitive advantage and increased cybersecurity costs. The article pays special attention to the role of cyber-espionage in the context of Russia’s war against Ukraine, where cyber operations have become an integral part of hybrid warfare. The article shows that cyber-attacks on Ukrainian government institutions, critical infrastructure, defence enterprises and economic entities pose security threats and are attempts to undermine economic resilience and acquire valuable strategic information. The study emphasises the challenges of international legal regulation and institutional responses to economic cyber-espionage. The lack of universally recognised rules governing state-sponsored cyber operations, the difficulty of attributing cyber attacks, and the limitations of international co-operation mechanisms all significantly reduce the effectiveness of countermeasures. The article concludes that economic cyber-espionage has become a significant factor in global economic security. In order to protect digital economies and ensure sustainable development, it is essential to strengthen international co-operation, develop unified regulatory approaches, improve cybersecurity governance and integrate cyber resilience into national economic strategies.

title: Dynamic resilience of China-Europe container maritime supply chains: data-driven measurement and configurational mechanisms
summary: Against growing global supply chain uncertainty and mandatory decarbonization regulations issued by the International Maritime Organization (IMO), China–Europe container maritime supply chains (CMSC) face continuous disruptions triggered by geopolitical conflicts, publichealth emergencies and trade frictions. Existing resilience studies are limited by ambiguous dimension classification and overreliance on static evaluation, and few datadriven assessment tools can simultaneously support risk governance and lowcarbon transition for sustainable shipping. This research addresses this research gap by establishing a coupled “capabilities–domains” framework for dynamic resilience evaluation of CMSC and forming a 12indicator system covering four resilience capabilities and three marketport domains. The overall resilience of CMSC presents an invertedU trend, rising first and then falling, with the peak observed during the RussiaUkraine conflict; resilience decreases by 2% in the Red Sea crisis, yet remains 13.4% higher than the level in the trade war period. Resistance (0.414) serves as the dominant capability in the trade war, recovery (0.510) reaches its maximum during the RussiaUkraine conflict, and adaptation and transformation capacities develop in tandem under lowcarbon pressure in the Red Sea crisis. Four distinct pathways for resilience enhancement are identified, among which the pathway of “recoverytransformation dualdrive under insufficient resistance” best explains the sustainable development of shipping systems. title: Perceived ESG disclosure and credit decision-making orientation: The mediating role of intention to use sustainability information in an emerging market
summary: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractIntegrating environmental, social, and governance factors into the credit granting process is an imperative requirement for financial risk management. This study aims to quantify the impact of the perceived corporate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) information disclosure on Credit Decision-Making Orientation and determine the mediating role of the intention to use sustainability information. Research data were collected through a survey of 235 credit officers and managers at 32 commercial banks in Vietnam from February to August 2024 and subsequently analyzed utilizing partial least squares structural equation modeling. The empirical results indicate that the disclosure levels of environmental, social, and governance information do not have a direct impact on credit decision-making orientation. However, these three factors positively affect the intention to use sustainability information, wherein the environmental factor exerts the most substantial influence (β = 0.447), followed by governance (β = 0.416) and social factors (β = 0.363). Furthermore, the intention to use sustainability information acts as a full mediator, exerting a strong positive impact on credit decision-making orientation (β = 0.558) and explaining 26.2% of the variance in the dependent variable. The study concludes that subjective credit appraisal orientations among banking personnel are primarily driven by their cognitive intention to integrate sustainability data rather than the mere presence of corporate disclosures.

title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transformation in Smart and Sustainable Infrastructure Systems
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and digitalization are rapidly transforming the planning, operation, maintenance and management of critical infrastructure. Planning, operation, maintenance and management of critical infrastructure is changing with Artificial Intelligence (AI) and digitalization. title: Integrated Framework of Key Facilitators, Motivators and Relief Aids for Flood Resilient Humanitarian Supply Chain
summary: This paper aims to identify, analyze, and prioritize the key supply chain facilitators, their associated motivators, and the relief aids that enable an agile, responsive and resilient Humanitarian Supply Chain (HSC) for flood relief, using Bihar (India) as a case study. A novel three-level decision hierarchy is proposed, consisting of supply chain facilitators as criteria, their associated motivators as sub-criteria, and relief aids as alternatives. A mixed-method approach is employed involving a comprehensive literature review, expert evaluations, and multi-criteria decision-making techniques of Best-Worst Method (BWM) and Technique for Order Performance by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS). Healthcare aids, followed by water and sanitation aids, and food aids are found as most critical humanitarian relief items during floods and should be prioritized, in that order, in emergency response operations. At the system level, quick response time and reduction of deprivation cost emerge as the most critical facilitators of HSC agility. These can be operationalized through motivators, namely, ensuring the availability of high-quality relief items, utilizing optimized transshipment and distribution routes, implementing effective reverse logistics, and reducing overall lead time. The study offers actionable insights for policymakers and practitioners to design and operate agile, resilient, and effective flood relief HSC; thereby mitigating the adverse impacts of flood disasters. This is the first study that conducts systematic research on HSC for flood relief in India, and first-ever study that identifies the key facilitators, motivators and relief aids for flood relief HSC. title: Strategic Workforce Planning for Sustainable Marketing: Aligning HR Talent Pipelines with Corporate ESG Commitments and Green Marketing Claims
summary: Abstract: As Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) mandates shift from peripheral corporate social responsibility initiatives to core strategic imperatives, organizations face increasing regulatory scrutiny and consumer backlash over "greenwashing." While green marketing claims are designed to convey sustainability commitments to external stakeholders, their authenticity depends heavily on the internal capabilities, ethical alignment, and strategic execution of the workforce. This paper examines the critical intersection of Strategic Workforce Planning (SWP) and sustainable marketing, investigating how human resource pipelines can be systematically aligned with corporate ESG commitments to ensure green claims remain credible, compliant, and operationally grounded. Integrating upper echelons theory, resource-based view (RBV), and sustainable Human Resource Management (sHRM) frameworks, this research explores the operational mechanisms required to build a sustainability-literate marketing workforce. It analyzes the entire employee life cycle—spanning targeted talent acquisition, ESG-aligned upskilling, performance management metrics, and cross-functional integration between HR, marketing, and sustainability compliance units. The study evaluates how gaps in internal sustainability competence contribute to greenwashing risks, deceptive claims, and subsequent reputational damage. The findings demonstrate that organizational alignment between HR pipelines and ESG strategies directly enhances green marketing performance, consumer trust, and corporate credibility. When marketing teams possess verified sustainability competencies and work within governance structures that reward ethical accuracy over exaggerated performance, green marketing strategies shift from superficial communication exercises to authentic value propositions. Conversely, misalignment between external marketing narrative and internal workforce capability creates operational disconnects that erode brand value. Ultimately, this paper offers a strategic operational model for chief human resources officers (CHROs) and chief marketing officers (CMOs) to co-design talent pipelines that insulate organizations against compliance risks while securing long-term competitive advantage through authentic green marketing.

title: A Multi Objective Sustainable Queuing Supply Chain Model with Learning Effects and Fuzzy Environment
summary: The present paper deals with a fuzzy-based supply chain model with the effect of learning for the supply chain under queuing theory, where carbon emission policies are allowed. Nowadays, carbon emissions affect the environment and ordering policies of industries. It is considered that storage items emit carbon units, and the carbon emission cost is included in this paper. The effect of learning reduces the total fuzzy cost per shipment during ordering policies, and the backordering cost and setup expenses follow the effect of learning, where the holding cost has been taken as fuzzy input parameters. The queuing concept is included in this model, and the proposed model is classified into three models under the learning effect. The manufacturer produces multiple items due to the multiple demands of the products from several buyers, and the produced items are stored in different warehouses. The total fuzzy cost is defuzzified with the help of the graded mean integration method under the proposed scenario, and the total cost function is compared with and without a fuzzy environment under the learning effect. For the justification of the proposed model, numerical examples have been presented, and a sensitivity analysis has also been presented to know about the changeable effect of inventory parameters that are involved in this model.

title: Environmental, social, and governance performance, analysts’ recommendations, coverage, and earnings forecast accuracy
summary: This study investigates whether environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance influences analysts’ recommendations, analyst coverage, and earnings forecast accuracy. Using a sample of 1,675 nonfinancial firms listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (TWSE) and Taipei Exchange (TPEx) from 2016 to 2023, we estimate regression models controlling for firm characteristics, corporate governance attributes, industry fixed effects, and year fixed effects. The results show that overall ESG performance is not significantly associated with analysts’ recommendation ratings, suggesting that analysts continue to rely primarily on traditional financial information when issuing investment recommendations. However, overall ESG performance is positively associated with analyst coverage, indicating that firms with stronger ESG performance attract greater analyst attention and research effort. Further analysis of the three ESG dimensions reveals that environmental performance is positively associated with analysts’ recommendation ratings, consistent with the view that strong environmental performance signals effective risk management and long-term competitiveness. In addition, social performance is negatively associated with both one-year and two-year absolute earnings forecast errors, suggesting that social-related ESG information improves the information environment and enhances analysts’ earnings forecast accuracy. These findings remain robust after controlling for industry and year fixed effects.

title: The Mediating Effect of Organisational Culture and Corporate Governance on Waste Minimisation in the Technical Seaworthiness Process in Sri Lankan Navy
summary: This quantitative study examines the impact of waste on the Sri Lanka Navy's (SLN) technical seaworthiness processes and the mediating roles of organisational culture and corporate governance. title: Regulatory penalties and ESG outcomes: a nonlinear governance mechanism
summary: This study examines the nonlinear relationship between environmental penalty intensity and corporate ESG performance, as well as the contextual conditions under which this relationship changes. Using panel data for Chinese A-share listed companies from 2013 to 2023, we employ a fixed-effects model, supplemented by instrumental variable, propensity score matching, and Heckman two-step approaches, to address potential endogeneity and sample selection concerns. The results reveal a significant U-shaped relationship between environmental penalty intensity and ESG performance: at low levels of penalty intensity, increased penalties suppress ESG performance, whereas beyond a critical threshold, further penalties promote ESG improvement. Further analyses show that this nonlinear effect is shaped by three moderating conditions. Media attention strengthens the positive segment of the U-shaped relationship by increasing external scrutiny and reputational pressure. Political connections weaken the governance effect of environmental penalties by buffering firms from regulatory and market discipline. Green technological innovation positively moderates the U-shaped relationship by enhancing firms’ internal capability to convert regulatory pressure into substantive environmental upgrading and ESG improvement. Heterogeneity analysis further indicates that the U-shaped relationship is more pronounced among firms with low goodwill, firms located in eastern regions, and firms facing lower financing constraints. This study contributes to the literature by moving beyond a linear perspective on environmental regulation and by identifying the external monitoring, institutional buffering, and internal capability conditions under which environmental penalties become effective governance mechanisms for improving ESG performance.

title: Digital Economy-Driven Skill Mismatch in Cross-Border E-Commerce
summary: This study develops a collaborative knowledge transfer framework to address skill mismatch in cross-border e-commerce under the digital economy. title: ADAPTIVE BUT FRAGMENTED: DISTRIBUTION AND LOGISTICS OF ASOPSI CULINARY MSMES FOR SUSTAINABLE SUPPLY CHAIN DEVELOPMENT
summary: This study maps the distribution and logistics configurations of culinary micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) affiliated with the Indonesian Beginner Entrepreneurs Association (ASOPSI) in South Tangerang and identifies the baseline gaps that must be addressed before developing a sustainable supply chain model. An exploratory qualitative case-study design was used. The present article draws on 11 in-depth MSME interviews documented on 14 August 2026, supported by field observations and project records. Data were analyzed through cross-case thematic coding, value-chain mapping, and gap analysis. The cases show four overlapping logistics configurations: order-responsive fresh production, frozen buffer-stock distribution, shelf-stable packaged distribution, and hybrid food-service distribution. Across these configurations, the supply chains are adaptive but fragmented. MSMEs use flexible sourcing, limited inventory, supplier delivery, self-delivery, app-based couriers, retail outlets, bazaars, social media, and business-to-business channels. Recurrent vulnerabilities involve raw-material price and quality volatility, perishability, packaging damage, returns, production bottlenecks, consignment-related working-capital lock-up, unstable market access, and limited logistics data visibility. Sustainable supply chain development should begin with simple logistics visibility, supplier and inventory discipline, fit-for-product delivery standards, market synchronization, and association-enabled coordination rather than immediately imposing complex formal systems. This baseline offers a practical foundation for the subsequent design of an association-based sustainable supply chain model.

title: The Impact of Global Supply Chain Disruption on Manufacturing and Service Industries: An Empirical Comparative Study
summary: Purpose: This study examines the multi-dimensional impacts of global supply chain disruptions across seven SCM domains and compares risk vulnerabilities between manufacturing and service industries.Methods: Based on survey data from 385 firms in China, non-parametric analyses were conducted following non-normality confirmation to evaluate disruption effects and inter-industry differences.Results: Global disruptions degraded six SCM domains, most severely logistics and supply management, while sustainability management uniquely improved. Manufacturing industry faced significantly higher risks in supply and logistics management than service industry due to physical supply chain dependencies. The remaining five domains showed no inter-industry differences, representing universal threats.Conclusion: This study shows that manufacturing and service industries experience supply chain crises differently due to their core business models. Manufacturing relies heavily on physical materials and global shipping, making it vulnerable to supply shortages and delivery delays. In contrast, service firms deal with intangible resources and can maintain operations using digital tools and local networks. Therefore, crisis management strategies must fit each industry's specific structure.

title: corporate artificial intelligence activity and accounting information comparability: evidence from CEO generational differences
summary: Accounting information comparability reflects not only common accounting standards but also the information-production process through which firms translate economic events into accounting outcomes. Using 12,355 firm-year observations for nonfinancial Chinese A-share listed firms from 2012 to 2022, we examine the relation between corporate AI activity and accounting information comparability. Our primary explanatory variable is the one-year-lagged standardized measure of ln(1 + AI patent applications)identified from patent classification codes, which captures firms’ verifiable AI technological capability. Firms with stronger AI capability exhibit greater accounting information comparability. Mechanism tests show that earlier AI activity is followed by stronger internal control and lower earnings management, both of which are associated with higher comparability. CEO cohort further shapes the organizational conversion of technological capability: the AI effect is stronger in firms led by CEOs born in 1970 or later. To assess the construct validity of the patent-based measure, we triangulate evidence from patents related to accounting information production, AI-related software and hardware investment, and AI signals in MD&A and annual reports. The relation between AI capability and comparability is stronger when firms make more explicit AI-related resource commitments and exhibit greater organizational attention to AI. The stronger effects among firms with greater analyst attention and higher internal coordination demands further point to the roles of external demand for comparable information and internal information-processing needs. The main findings are robust to alternative measures, double machine learning, a policy-exposure instrumental-variable design, and entropy balancing. Overall, the evidence shows how AI technological capability can translate into more comparable accounting information through information production, organizational embedding, and managerial influence.

title: Methodological approach to the digital transformation of university business processes for interaction with applicants
summary: The article develops a methodological approach to the digital transformation of university business processes for interaction with applicants. title: Navigating Digital Transformation: Sociological and Educational Factors in Corporate AI Strategy Adoption
summary: To address the practical challenge of the disconnect between AI strategy implementation and performance outcomes in enterprises, this study focuses on the three-dimensional execution mechanism encompassing "resourcesprocess-culture," examining its mediating role between AI strategies and corporate performance, as well as the moderating effects of firm size and industry characteristics. Data were collected via random sampling using the Wenjuanxing online survey platform, supplemented by a 12-month longitudinal case tracking study. Empirical analysis employed structural equation modeling, grouped regression, and interaction term testing. Results demonstrate that the three-dimensional execution mechanism fully mediates the relationship between AI strategies and corporate performance, with resource allocation playing the most significant mediating role. Firm size positively moderates the performance effect of the execution mechanism, with large firms exhibiting significantly better implementation outcomes than small and medium-sized enterprises. Industry characteristics exhibit heterogeneity: technology-intensive industries show stronger positive impacts of the execution mechanism compared to non-technology-intensive sectors. Differentiation in implementation pathways reveals adaptability— technology-intensive firms benefit from a "resource priority or lightweight resources plus cultural guidance" approach, while non-technology-intensive firms are better suited for a "culture priority plus lightweight processes" model. This study evaluates AI strategy implementation primarily through organizational financial and innovation performance indicators. Although these metrics serve as organizational-level proxies for implementation effectiveness, they do not directly measure employee-level social outcomes, such as workplace learning, well-being, psychological safety, re-skilling, or perceived equity; therefore, the social implications discussed in this study should be interpreted within this scope.

title: Does Green Innovation Alleviate or Aggravate Financing Constraints? — Uncovering a Nonlinear Threshold Effect: Evidence from Chinese Listed Firms
summary: Green innovation has been a highly debated topic, which is increasingly important for market entities, especially firms and policy makers. Nevertheless, the advancement of green innovation is constrained by its inherent characteristics: high upfront investment, long payback periods, and substantial risks. This paper selects Chinese A-share listed companies from 2015 to 2024 as the initial research sample, and elaborates on the nonlinear relationship between corporate green innovation (measured by green patent counts) and financing constraints represented by the SA index, filling the research gap in existing relevant studies and providing solid empirical evidence to support the formulation, implementation and optimization of green innovation supporting policies. Using panel data, fixed-effects models, and heterogeneity tests, this study examines the inverted U-shaped relationship between green innovation and financing constraints. The findings offer empirical clarification on how green innovation alleviates financing constraints, and carry meaningful implications for stimulating market vitality and advancing high-quality green transformation.

title: Role Of Fintech in Indian Banking Industry
summary: Abstract Fintech has played a key role in boosting India's financial ecosystem through digitalization of loans, payments, and regulatory issues, which are changing the way the banking sector operates. Fintech, or financial technology, has grown in significance on a worldwide scale as it transforms how people and companies engage with financial services. Fintech uses technology to improve financial services' accessibility, efficiency, transparency, and innovation, which benefits a variety of users in many industries. Millions more Indians now have better access to financial services via digital and mobile platforms thanks to the quick development of financial technology, or fintech. This descriptive study examines the factors that have contributed to the emergence of fintech, the different kinds of fintech apps, the obstacles that fintech applications face in India and the prospects for the future.

title: Navigating Bureaucratic Disruption: Organizational Adaptation in the Digital Transformation of E-Planning in Surabaya
summary: Background: Digital transformation has become a strategic agenda for public administration reform. However, previous research has focused more on the adoption of technology and its successful implementation than on the dynamics of organizational change after digitalization. Objective: This study analyzes bureaucratic disruption due to the implementation of e-planning and the process of adaptation of local government organizations to these changes. Methods: This study used a qualitative case-study design in the Surabaya City Government. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with informants from BAPPEDA and DISKOMINFO, observations of e-planning use, planning coordination meetings, and program and activity preparation, and analysis of the RPJMD 2021–2026, Mayor Regulation No. 62 of 2023, RKPD 2025, and LKPJ 2025. ATLAS.ti was used to analyze the interview transcripts and policy documents through open coding, axial coding, and network analysis. Results: The findings indicate that e-planning implementation was accompanied by changes in workflows, distribution of authority, digital competency needs, and apparatus resistance. Across the case data, bureaucratic disruption appeared as a transitional condition associated with organizational responses such as strengthening e-planning, adjusting procedures, improving human resource competence, organizational learning, cross-agency coordination, digital culture, and bureaucratic simplification. Conclusion: The case findings indicate that digital transformation in Surabaya involves both technological and organizational change. Based on patterns across the analyzed sources, this study proposes a conceptual model in which bureaucratic disruption is interpreted as a transitional phase associated with organizational adaptation. This model represents a case-based conceptual interpretation rather than a demonstrated causal mechanism.

title: Colonial Environmental Governance in Maluku (1652–1799): Historical Insights from Hongi Tochten
summary: The Dutch East India Company (VOC) maintained its clove monopoly in the Maluku Islands through Hongi Tochten, a series of naval expeditions traditionally interpreted as instruments of military coercion and commercial control. However, their role as mechanisms of environmental governance has received limited scholarly attention. This study examines how Hongi Tochten unctioned as a system of colonial environmental governance and analyses its implications for indigenous social–ecological systems in Maluku between 1652 and 1799. Using a qualitative historical approach, the study analyses VOC archival records, colonial administrative documents, and relevant historical literature through the analytical lenses of colonial environmental governance, ecological regulation, and social–ecological systems. These findings demonstrate that historical analysis can contribute to contemporary environmental governance by revealing the long-term institutional and ecological consequences of colonial resource regulation. These interventions transformed indigenous production systems, customary resource governance, and local livelihoods, while simultaneously generating adaptive responses, including the concealment and relocation of clove seedlings, livelihood diversification, informal trade, and the preservation of ecological knowledge. These findings demonstrate that Hongi Tochten functioned as an institutional system of colonial environmental governance through which ecological regulation became a central mechanism of imperial authority. Beyond contributing to environmental history, the study provides historical insights for contemporary environmental governance by demonstrating the long-term consequences of ecological regulation for indigenous social–ecological systems, sustainable resource governance, and environmental decision-making.

title: Ketahanan rantai pasokan dan digitalisasi: Peran mediasi manajemen risiko terhadap kinerja rantai pasokan pada perusahaan manufaktur
summary: This study examines how supply chain resilience and supply chain digitalization influence supply chain performance, with supply chain risk management acting as a mediating variable in manufacturing companies in Indonesia. The research is driven by growing uncertainty in global supply chains and the need for firms to build adaptive and technology-enabled capabilities to maintain operational continuity and competitiveness. A quantitative approach was adopted, and primary data were collected through a survey of 150 employees who are directly involved in supply chain activities across various departments in Indonesian manufacturing firms. The data were analyzed using a structural equation modeling technique to assess the relationships among the key constructs. The findings show that companies with stronger resilience capabilities tend to achieve better supply chain outcomes. Similarly, firms that more extensively adopt digital technologies in their supply chains are better positioned to enhance performance. The results also indicate that effective supply chain risk management, plays an important role in strengthening the benefits of resilience and digitalization. Overall, the study suggests that manufacturing firms should view resilience, digitalization, and risk management as strategically interconnected capabilities that work together to improve supply chain performance in an increasingly uncertain business environment. Penelitian ini mengkaji bagaimana ketahanan rantai pasokan dan digitalisasi rantai pasokan memengaruhi kinerja rantai pasokan, dengan manajemen risiko rantai pasokan berperan sebagai variabel mediasi pada perusahaan manufaktur di Indonesia. Studi ini dilatarbelakangi oleh meningkatnya ketidakpastian dalam rantai pasokan global dan kebutuhan perusahaan untuk membangun kapabilitas yang adaptif serta berbasis teknologi guna menjaga keberlangsungan operasi dan daya saing. Pendekatan kuantitatif digunakan, dengan data primer yang dikumpulkan melalui survei terhadap 150 karyawan yang terlibat langsung dalam aktivitas rantai pasokan di berbagai departemen perusahaan manufaktur Indonesia. Data dianalisis menggunakan teknik pemodelan persamaan struktural untuk menilai hubungan antar konstruk utama. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa perusahaan dengan kemampuan ketahanan yang kuat akan cenderung mencapai kinerja rantai pasokan yang lebih baik. Demikian pula, perusahaan yang mengadopsi teknologi digital berada pada posisi yang lebih baik untuk meningkatkan kinerja. Temuan juga mengindikasikan bahwa manajemen risiko rantai pasokan berperan penting dalam memperkuat manfaat dari ketahanan dan digitalisasi. Secara keseluruhan, penelitian ini menyarankan agar perusahaan manufaktur memandang ketahanan, digitalisasi, dan manajemen risiko sebagai kapabilitas strategis yang saling terhubung dan bekerja bersama untuk meningkatkan kinerja rantai pasokan dalam lingkungan bisnis yang semakin tidak pasti.

title: Miniaturising judgement: Key Performance Indicators as psychotechnologies of transition
summary: Abstract This article examines how key performance indicators (KPIs) organise professional judgement and collective agency in green finance. Drawing on multi-sited ethnographic fieldwork conducted between 2020 and 2023, it brings together observation of International Capital Market Association working groups, training for emerging climate-fund managers, practitioner interviews, and sustained use of Refinitiv’s Eikon terminal. It develops miniaturisation as an account of how extended, contested judgements are condensed into portable signs: scores, certification flags, icons, and diagrammatic sequences. These forms make sustainability judgements readily available for comparison and action while conveying institutional decisions whose premises become harder to inspect. Following Stiegler, the article approaches KPI infrastructures as psychotechnologies of transition: technical arrangements that shape attention, memory, and the capacity to judge. A trophy icon directs users towards selected data; a binary certification field makes a review’s qualifications less visible; a theory-of-change diagram connects present investment to anticipated benefits. These devices also sustain professional commitment by giving practitioners ways to act towards otherwise overwhelming climate futures. Their enchantment lies in making shared courses of action credible and practicable. The analysis shows how this capacity to coordinate action coexists with unequal opportunities to define and revise its technical conditions. Practitioners retain expertise while participating unevenly in the production of the categories and pathways through which they work. The article locates the stakes of KPI-based green finance in this separation between the collective capacity to act and the capacity to shape what transition should mean.

title: Board Diversity Effect on Earnings Management among Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Palestine, and the United Arab Emirates
summary: Purpose: The purpose of this research is to investigate the effects of board diversity and board composition on earnings management of publicly traded non-financial firms in the Middle East institutional and regulatory environment (Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Palestine and UAE). Design/Methodology/Approach: This study used a panel dataset from 2013-2023 of 2,937 observations to analyze how board diversity (Board Diversity Index) affects earnings management (Modified Jones Model) in 258 non-financial listed companies in Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Palestine, and the United Arab Emirates. Findings: The results show that board diversity positively affects earnings management in a statistically significant manner, for the three quantiles (25th, 50th, 75th), however the most pronounced impact is found in the lowest quantile. Therefore, it is clear that board diversity does not always result in reduced earnings management, but rather the level of governance effectiveness provided by board diversity depends upon the institutional and governance environments in which the organization operates. Implications/Originality/Value: Board diversity may or may not help with the reduction of earnings management within middle eastern firms; however, this study demonstrates how institutional context is key to understanding the relationship between the two and adds to the growing body of literature on emerging markets

title: Green finance and agricultural carbon reduction drive rural revitalization through spatial spillovers in western China
summary: Rural revitalization is critical for constructing a modern socialist nation and ecological civilization. Focusing on western China, this study employs a spatial econometric model to investigate how green finance and agricultural carbon emission reduction influence rural revitalization through spatial spillover effects. Empirical results reveal distinct "Low-Low" and "High-Low" spatial agglomeration patterns. Significantly, green finance and carbon reduction demonstrate positive spatial spillover effects, comprehensively promoting rural revitalization. The robustness of these findings is validated through varied spatial weight matrices and heterogeneity analyses across ethnic provinces and ecological phases. Based on these empirical insights, the study proposes policy recommendations to enhance environmental regulation frameworks and foster the synergistic advancement of green finance and low-carbon agriculture. These measures aim to address inadequate regional development and facilitate high-quality economic growth.

title: Analisis Komparatif Penerapan Keuangan Berkelanjutan Berbasis ESG dan Implikasinya Terhadap Nilai Perusahaan pad PT Unilever Indonesia TBK dan PT Indofood Sukses Makmur TBK
summary: This research aims to analyze the comparative implementation of sustainable finance based on Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) and its impact on company value at PT Unilever Indonesia Tbk and PT Indofood Berhasil Makmur Tbk. The method used in this study is qualitative with a descriptive comparative approach. The information used is secondary data drawn from the annual reports and sustainability reports of both companies. The analytical methods employed include content analysis, comparative analysis, and interpretive analysis with reference to stakeholder theory. The findings of this research indicate that PT Unilever Indonesia Tbk has a higher and more strategic level of ESG implementation compared to PT Indofood Berhasil Makmur Tbk, which focuses more on operational aspects. ESG implementation at Unilever serves as a value driver, increasing company value through reputation and investor confidence. Meanwhile, at Indofood, ESG implementation serves more as a risk management tool, so its impact on company value is indirect. The conclusions of this research emphasize that the level of ESG integration in business strategy can influence the increase in company value. As ESG continues to be integrated into industry activities, it continues to make a significant contribution to generating long-term value.

title: Understanding Indonesian Consumer Responses in the Digital Economy: A Lens of The Information Adoption Model
summary: This research examines marketing communication patterns in electronic commerce (e-commerce) in the big data era that can influence customer online behavior. This study employs the Information Adoption Model to explain the developed research framework. Data were collected using a questionnaire distributed to 338 e-marketplace users in Indonesia selected through a purposive sampling technique. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Square (SEM-PLS) with a Path Analysis approach by SMART-PLS. This study indicates that advertisements customized with information about incentives and delivered through a quality platform are considered as appropriate information, encouraging customer behavior to click on advertisements. This study recommends that marketers develop customer communication strategies aligned with the era of big data. To gain positive customers’ responses or benefit marketers in the big data era, an effective online advertising strategy should utilize customer profile data and their product traces to create customized offer information that is delivered at the right time and benefit the customers. There are many factors that need to be elaborated regarding online advertising and consumer behavior. In addition, this study does not classify customers based on ages, making it difficult to analyze customer behavior based on generations.

title: Selling mode strategy and streamer choice in a live-streaming supply chain considering product returns
summary: Live-streaming e-commerce has revolutionised retail by enabling real-time interactions between brand owners, streamers, and consumers, which makes it an indispensable marketing tool for today’s brand owners. Considering the various types of streamers and high possibility of product returns in live-streaming, this study explores optimal strategies for brand owners in choosing live-streaming selling modes and streamers for product promotion. We find that no strategy is universally superior: the best choice depends on return costs, bargaining power, the streamer’s influence, and pit fees. Commission-based collaboration is more effective for influential streamers, especially if the cost of return is not high. In contrast, using employee streamers can be more profitable when the return cost is high or brands possess strong bargaining power. Notably, our research indicates that brand owners can still achieve profit when partnering with highly influential streamers, even if they give up pricing power, absorb return costs, and pay streamer commissions. This study provides crucial insights for brand owners in live-streaming e-commerce regarding streamer selection, mode choice, and effective management of returns.

title: Dynamics and coordination of water and carbon footprints in China, 2007–2023: drivers and supply-chain pathways
summary: Coordinated water and carbon management requires identifying not only whether the two environmental pressures change in the same direction, but also which socioeconomic drivers and supply-chain pathways generate co-benefits or trade-offs. Existing studies rarely integrate temporal driver decomposition with pathway-level diagnosis of paired water- and carbon-footprint changes. Using China’s benchmark input-output tables for 2007–2023, we integrated environmentally extended input-output analysis, structural decomposition analysis, structural path decomposition, and a coordination assessment. From 2012 to 2023, China’s consumption-based water footprint decreased from 555.08 to 497.04 billion m³ (− 10.46%), whereas its carbon footprint increased from 9,336.06 to 10,963.28 Mt CO₂ (+ 17.43%). Urban household consumption remained the principal carrier of the water footprint and became an increasingly important source of carbon growth, while fixed capital formation continued to sustain carbon-intensive demand. The final-demand scale effect generated co-increases in every subperiod, whereas direct-intensity and production-structure effects more often contributed to co-reductions but were not uniformly aligned across periods and sectors. Water-footprint changes were concentrated in agriculture- and food-related pathways, whereas carbon-footprint changes were more strongly associated with electricity and heat supply, materials, construction, and capital formation. These distinct supply-chain backbones explain why water-saving improvements did not automatically produce parallel carbon mitigation. The post-2012 decline in China’s water footprint cannot be interpreted as evidence of simultaneous carbon mitigation. By separating directional coordination states from relative responses and tracing them to specific drivers and supply-chain pathways, this study identifies where integrated water–carbon intervention is feasible and where separate controls remain necessary. Effective management should coordinate agriculture–food water-saving measures with the decarbonization of electricity-, materials-, construction-, and investment-related supply chains.

title: Blockchain Enabled Circular Supply Chain Management for Product Lifecycle Tracking and Consumer Incentives: A Case Study in Sri Lanka
summary: Closing the post-consumer loop remains a persistent challenge in waste management and pollution control. While blockchain technology has improved upstream traceability, most systems terminate tracking at the point of sale, leaving consumer disposal undocumented. This blind spot undermines circular economy implementation, limits Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) compliance, and exacerbates municipal solid waste pollution. This study addresses this gap by developing a blockchain-enabled tracking framework that integrates an immutable ledger for life cycle tracking, a consumer mobile application for disposal registration, and IoT-enabled smart disposal machines to verify physical waste recovery events. The system’s technical feasibility was validated through a functional prototype and Minimum Viable Product (MVP) blockchain validation, confirming efficient transaction handling and secure life cycle updates. Furthermore, socio-technical factors driving user adoption of this green technology were evaluated using an empirical survey (*r* = .72, *p* < .001) and stakeholder interviews. This research provides an enhanced framework incorporating Digital Product Passports (DPP) to improve global material recovery and reduce environmental contamination. The system architecture is evaluated across high-impact waste streams including fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG), automotive parts, and electronic waste (mobile phones) while contextualizing regional regulatory challenges against global sustainability standards. Visual diagrams and policy comparison analyses support a clearer understanding of life cycle traceability and tech-driven pollution mitigation. These contributions offer a validated, scalable framework that organizations can leverage to enhance consumer participation, improve material recovery, and enable data-driven environmental management.

summary: Abstract The rapid development of digital technologies has transformed modern society in almost every sphere of human life. title: Auditable Admissibility: Ultimate Explanation and the Selection of Candidates
summary: Recent grounding-theoretic work has produced increasingly rigorous certifications of rival ultimate explainers — necessary beings, autonomous essences, trans-categorial grounds, strongly well-founded structures — while the most developed comparative methodology for global theories, Oppy's virtue-theoretic naturalism, acknowledges the incompleteness of its own metric across multi-dimensional trade-offs. We argue that this acknowledged limit becomes acute precisely where the later grounding-theoretic candidates would have to be compared, and that the two literatures fail to mesh for a structural reason. Distinguishing three tasks — structural admissibility, candidate identification, and cross-framework selection — we show that every account examined here resolves, defers, asserts, or concedes the third task without an articulated account of the transition from intra-framework certification to cross-framework selection under conditions of policy disagreement. Our central claim: if cross-framework selection is to represent rather than merely dissolve disagreement, it requires an explicit admissibility policy whose commitments are publicly auditable and dialectically revisable; the accounts examined here leave that policy implicit, defer it, or defend it only within the framework whose candidates it licenses. The paper introduces the concept of an admissibility policy — the entry conditions, explanandum registry, and translation rules that constitute any comparison's space — and specifies the minimal representational architecture such a policy requires, including a detachable instrument, dual-ledger cost accounting, without prejudging how comparative judgment then falls.

title: From pipeline to policy: designing India's Article 6 approval framework for climate finance and domestic decarbonisation
summary: Article 6 of the Paris Agreement offers India an opportunity to receive payments from other countries for mitigation outcomes at home, and to channel that revenue towards the vast investment that the low-carbon transition requires. Yet while the country can use international carbon markets to help finance its own decarbonisation, it will need to establish the right framework for approving sales of its Article 6 projects. Without this, there is a risk that India will undermine efforts to hit its near-term climate targets and achieve its 2070 net zero goal. This report explores how the country can establish such a framework. The author argues that India should decide whether to authorise sales of carbon credits under Article 6 based on calibrated questions about what to sell, when to sell it and at what price.

title: Does negative environmental performance feedback affect corporate green innovation? Evidence from China
summary: Purpose Previous research on performance feedback has mainly focused on financial performance feedback, largely overlooking environmental performance feedback. This paper aims to explore the impact of negative environmental performance feedback on corporate green innovation and its underlying mechanism. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the behavioral theory of the firm, this study uses data from Chinese listed manufacturing firms from 2010 to 2022 to examine the relationship between negative environmental performance feedback and corporate green innovation through ordinary least squares regression analysis. Findings The results show that negative environmental performance feedback has a U-shaped effect on corporate green innovation. This relationship is mediated by executive environmental attention. Furthermore, environmental regulation negatively moderates the relationship between negative environmental performance feedback and corporate green innovation. Originality/value This study contributes to the performance feedback literature by revealing how negative environmental performance feedback influences corporate green innovation.

title: Development Sharia Investment in Indonesia in the Digital Era
summary: This study aims to analyze the development of sharia investment in Indonesia in the digital era, including the sharia capital market, sharia fintech, and investment instrument innovations. The study employed a library research method with a qualitative descriptive approach based on relevant academic literature. The findings show that digitalization has accelerated the growth of sharia investment through easier access, transaction efficiency, and innovations such as sharia fintech, online sharia mutual funds, and digital sukuk. Digitalization has also increased financial inclusion and public investment interest, particularly among younger generations. However, challenges remain, including low levels of sharia financial literacy, limited product diversification, cybersecurity risks, and technological infrastructure disparities. The study concludes that the digital era provides significant opportunities for the development of sharia investment in Indonesia, but sustainable growth requires supportive regulations, improved sharia financial literacy, and stronger digital infrastructure.

title: Determinants of ESG Disclosure Quality in an Emerging Market: The Role of Firm and Governance Characteristics
summary: This study examines the determinants of Environment, Social and Governance (ESG) disclosure quality among companies listed on the South Pacific Stock Exchange (SPX), with particular emphasis on quality rather than quantity of ESG information disclosed. Using panel data from SPX-listed companies for 2016 to 2024, the study assesses ESG disclosure quality through a structured content analysis of annual reports, guided by a multi-construct evaluation framework. The final measurement model retains eight environmental and social disclosure items and excludes four governance items that did not meet convergent-validity requirements, so the ESG Disclosure Quality construct reflects environmental and social disclosure quality rather than the full governance dimension of ESG. The study tests hypothesised relationships between firm characteristics, governance mechanisms, and ESG disclosure quality using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that firm size, industry sector, and board size are significantly associated with ESG disclosure quality, whereas profitability, leverage, board independence, and audit quality show no significant association. These results suggest that organisational visibility and governance capacity play a more important role in shaping ESG disclosure quality than financial performance. The study contributes to the growing ESG disclosure literature by providing evidence from a small-island emerging market (Fiji) that remains underrepresented in sustainability reporting research. The findings are interpreted through Salient Stakeholder Theory, suggesting that organisational visibility and governance capacity function as observable proxies for stakeholder salience in a frontier market context, although the theory’s core attributes of stakeholder power, legitimacy, and urgency are not directly measured in this study.

title: AI-ENABLED DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AND COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGE IN SMES: A STRATEGIC ANALYSIS WITHIN THE SPANISH BUSINESS ECOSYSTEM
summary: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are increasingly adopting artificial intelligence (AI) to improve operational efficiency, strengthen innovation capabilities, and sustain long-term competitiveness. Within the Spanish business ecosystem, digital transformation has accelerated over the past decade due to technological progress, evolving customer expectations, and supportive national and European digitalization policies. Nevertheless, the adoption of AI among Spanish SMEs remains uneven, with significant differences across sectors, organizational capabilities, and regional innovation environments. This study examines how AI-driven digital transformation contributes to competitive advantage in Spanish SMEs from a strategic management perspective. Rather than treating AI as a standalone technological solution, the paper considers it an organizational capability that reshapes decision-making, resource allocation, customer engagement, and business model innovation. The discussion integrates perspectives from the resource-based view, dynamic capability theory, digital transformation research, and innovation management to explain the strategic mechanisms through which AI creates sustainable value. Particular attention is given to organizational readiness, leadership, digital culture, workforce skills, data governance, and ecosystem collaboration. The study also evaluates the challenges that continue to limit AI implementation, including financial constraints, technological complexity, cybersecurity concerns, regulatory compliance, and shortages of digital talent. The findings suggest that sustainable competitive advantage depends not solely on technological investment but on the ability of SMEs to integrate AI into strategic planning, organizational learning, and continuous innovation processes. The Spanish experience demonstrates that successful AI adoption emerges from the interaction between internal capabilities and external institutional support, providing valuable insights for SMEs operating in similar economic environments.

title: Aligning Financial Education with the National Education Policy: Towards a Strategic Framework for Developing Informed Capital Market Investors
summary: Indian Capital Markets have demonstrated strong performance and have been instrumental in economic prosperity over the years. title: Carbon Cost Information Collection and Consolidation from an ESG Perspective: A Case Study of Kingfa
summary: Purpose: To examine how carbon cost information is collected and consolidated from an Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) perspective, using Kingfa Science & Technology as a case study. Specifically, the study aims to address the fragmentation of carbon-related physical and financial data across corporate systems and to construct a practical framework for carbon cost classification, attribution, and consolidation, thereby supporting the "dual-carbon" goals and responding to external pressures such as the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM). Methodology: This study adopts a single-case study approach based on publicly available secondary data, including Kingfa's annual reports (2022–2025), sustainability reports (2022–2025), and the China Carbon Market Development Report (2025). Data analysis employs trend comparison to track the co-movement of green business expansion and carbon intensity changes, and monetary conversion estimation using market reference prices to bridge physical energy consumption data with financial cost information. The analysis covers Scope 1 (direct emissions) and Scope 2 (energy indirect emissions), with Scope 3 addressed qualitatively by materiality, since public reporting provides it only as an unverified group-level aggregate that cannot be attributed to a cost object. Findings: The study reveals that Kingfa's carbon cost information is highly fragmented across ESG, energy, production, R&D, and financial systems, with no effective mapping between physical emission data and financial cost data. Three major gaps are identified: (1) inconsistent classification and accounting boundaries of carbon costs; (2) lack of mapping between physical and monetary data; and (3) unclear cost objects and cost drivers. To address these gaps, the study proposes a carbon cost collection and consolidation mechanism comprising: (a) a three-tier classification framework dividing carbon costs into carbon emission costs, carbon abatement costs, and carbon risk costs; (b) a tripartite "cost object–cost driver–responsibility center" consolidation structure that clarifies cost attribution, allocation basis, and accountable entities. Unique Contribution to Theory, Practice and Policy: The proposed mechanism enhances the traceability and managerial relevance of carbon cost information, filling the research gap on front-end information collection and consolidation from an ESG perspective. For practice, it provides Kingfa and similar manufacturing enterprises with a structured approach to integrating fragmented carbon data into managerial decision-making. For policy, the study offers empirical insights for regulators and standard-setters to consider enterprise-level carbon cost accounting frameworks that align with both domestic "dual-carbon" targets and international mechanisms such as CBAM.

title: Road Safety as a Supply Chain Vulnerability in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Structured Literature Review and Conceptual Framework for the Zimbabwean Context
summary: Road safety is widely recognised as a public health and transport challenge; however, its role as a strategic determinant of supply chain vulnerability remains underexplored. This study reviews how road safety influences supply chain vulnerability in sub-Saharan Africa and develops a conceptual framework that positions road safety as an endogenous source of supply chain disruption. A structured literature review of 87 peer-reviewed studies published between 2000 and 2026 was conducted using the PRISMA protocol and thematic analysis. Four interacting vulnerability drivers were identified: infrastructure inadequacy, driver behaviour and fatigue, poor vehicle fleet condition, and weak regulatory enforcement. These drivers increase crash risk, disrupt freight movement, and generate operational, financial, and strategic vulnerabilities. Resilience capabilities, including visibility, collaboration, digital technologies, and proactive risk management, moderate these vulnerabilities through organisational learning and institutional feedback. The study contributes an integrated causal conceptualisation linking road safety risks, freight disruption, supply chain vulnerability, resilience capabilities, and institutional feedback. The framework supports future research and efforts to strengthen resilient freight systems in sub-Saharan Africa.

title: Bridging Model Sophistication and Managerial Adoption: A Structured Review of Operations Research in FMCG Supply Chain Optimisation
summary: Operations research (OR) has long supported supply chain decisions for fast moving consumer goods (FMCG), a sector marked by thin margins, short shelf lives, demand that swings with promotions and highly fragmented retail. This review examines whether OR models capture these features and whether richer models reach practice. We analyse 22 peer reviewed applications published between 1994 and 2024, coding each model against seven defining characteristics of FMCG to form an FMCG Specificity Index, and against a four level scale of adoption evidence. Nineteen of the 22 models extend the classical transportation problem. Mean specificity is low, at 2.09 out of 7: promotions are modelled in one study and demand uncertainty in four. Adoption evidence is not significantly related to specificity (Spearman ρ = −0.21, p = 0.36) but tends to decline as solution methods grow more complex (ρ = −0.37, p = 0.12). All five implemented models rely on exact methods or constructive heuristics, whereas none of the six metaheuristic models reports implementation. We therefore propose simplicity preserving specificity as a design principle and demonstrate it with real promotion data from a US grocery retailer. The resulting FMCG Fractile Method can be applied in a spreadsheet, matches the optimal stochastic plan to within 0.005 percent of expected cost, and reduces expected cost by 13 to 57 percent relative to planning that ignores promotions. The review closes with a research agenda and a reporting checklist for FMCG optimisation studies.
